mbm-0851.clue: I went out for a lampshade.
mbm-0851.quote: I came back from the flea market with an enormous green glass lampshade. The seller also threw in the lamp and a ride home. Mum had to take down a shelf to let the thing shine.

mbm-0852.clue: My ski partner knows the sound of my laugh.
mbm-0852.quote: Fog rolled over the last bend and I lost sight of my brother. At the lift I heard him laughing at the snow piled on my helmet. I’d been looking for him two chairs ahead.

mbm-0853.clue: I stitched a shortcut to school.
mbm-0853.quote: I quilted the blocks around my first school in bright checks. The gap in the fence got one little buttonhole, exactly where our book bags used to squeeze through.

mbm-0854.clue: I can hear a sandwich opening.
mbm-0854.quote: Our rafting crew kept perfectly quiet on the smooth stretch to see a heron. Then my stomach growled. The heron stayed put and six people passed me half a sandwich.

mbm-0855.clue: I sewed a pocket just for the stone.
mbm-0855.quote: My niece brought home a heart-shaped pebble. I put a tiny velvet pocket in her jacket for it. If you ask about the bulge she makes you promise to wash your hands first.

mbm-0856.clue: I’ve watched a bird wait for the traffic light.
mbm-0856.quote: A crow dropped a walnut at the crossing and waited on the traffic signal. I had my binoculars on it when the shell opened. It looked both ways longer than I did.

mbm-0857.clue: My best shirt has a crooked sunrise.
mbm-0857.quote: I made a shirt with a bright sun peeking above the breast pocket. I put it on and found the horizon sloped downhill. My sister asked me to sew hers just as crooked.

mbm-0858.clue: I take my breakfast with two googly eyes.
mbm-0858.quote: I crocheted a little fried egg with a smiling yellow center as a potholder. It hangs by the skillet. Somehow I feel like a better cook with an audience that easy to please.

mbm-0859.clue: I learned to let go at the right time.
mbm-0859.quote: At the end of my water-ski run I let the tow handle fall and coasted toward the dock. My nephew raised his toy steering wheel like he’d personally brought me in.

mbm-0860.quote: The little elephant at our mini-golf course lost its trunk to a storm. I helped the owner paint its new one pink. I give it a tap for luck every time I play the hole.

mbm-0861.clue: I left a fingerprint in the handle.
mbm-0861.quote: My pottery teacher offered to smooth the thumbprint off my coffee mug. I kept it. Every morning my thumb falls into the same little groove before I’m fully awake.

mbm-0862.clue: I found out how much a cloud weighs.
mbm-0862.quote: I carried my niece’s stuffed cloud up the trail when she got tired. At the overlook we held it up to the sky. In her photo it looks big enough to rain on the whole valley.

mbm-0863.clue: I kept the moon from opening night.
mbm-0863.quote: I painted a cardboard moon for our theater’s balcony scene. The string broke and I had to hold it up myself. From the wings I got the best view of two very surprised lovers.

mbm-0864.clue: I’m a terrible judge of tentacles.
mbm-0864.quote: I crocheted a purple octopus and counted nine legs after I’d sewn them on. My nephew called the last one a spare. He thinks all the real octopuses are underprepared.

mbm-0865.clue: I like the back of the museum staircase.
mbm-0865.quote: A carved fox hides beneath the handrail in our local museum. The guide caught me sketching it and showed me the tiny rabbit on the other side. I’ve been looking under stairs ever since.

mbm-0866.clue: I owe my winning shot to a sneaker.
mbm-0866.quote: My mini-golf ball stopped beside my cousin’s enormous sneaker at the pirate ship. He stood perfectly still until I putted past his toe, then charged me one ice cream for the harbor fee.

mbm-0867.clue: I can fold the whole night shift.
mbm-0867.quote: I made a quilt from the blue and violet shirts my mum wore on night duty. The one bright square is yellow, the color of our kitchen when she got home for breakfast.

mbm-0868.clue: I gave our dog his own weather.
mbm-0868.quote: I quilted a little rain cloud above his water bowl and a striped sun above his bed. He drags the sun square into the garden whenever the real weather disappoints him.

mbm-0869.clue: I paint the backs of my cards.
mbm-0869.quote: I painted little lanterns on my fantasy-card sleeves. When I spread them in a circle it looks like a village at night. My opponent always asks to turn the lights down for the first deal.

mbm-0870.clue: I keep the apple cores in a jar.
mbm-0870.quote: Our quilt guild calls those curved scraps apple cores. I made a whole picnic blanket from them. My dad looked puzzled when I carried it outside without a single apple.

mbm-0871.clue: I recognize that plane by its shadow.
mbm-0871.quote: On the airfield footpath I sketched wings as they passed across the concrete. My friend checked my guesses against the planes at the hangars. I got the one with the crooked wingtip light.

mbm-0872.clue: My first landing is still in my sock drawer.
mbm-0872.quote: I landed in a meadow after my tandem jump and picked a tiny yellow flower off my shoelace. The pressed flower has outlasted the shoes and every single boast I made beforehand.

mbm-0873.clue: I read with a postcard as a compass.
mbm-0873.quote: My aunt sent me a seaside postcard with a detective novel. Whenever the detective crossed the pier I turned the card around, as if the culprit might be standing on the other side.

mbm-0874.clue: I made a bowl for a very small storm.
mbm-0874.quote: I swirled two blue glazes into the bottom of a bowl. When I pour in soup a little white spiral peeks above the surface. My sister calls it the forecast.

mbm-0875.clue: I always take a spare pencil to anime club.
mbm-0875.quote: We paused a tape to draw the hero’s dramatic cape. The VCR ate the tape halfway through. Everyone finished from memory, and our capes all blew in completely different directions.
